homonyms.basis: The census row carries no disambiguation field. No card is a homonym, and T composes no other entity under the name: its 'About the Trust' part composes the archive's holder, a distinct entity the field itself sets beside the archive (the archive's pages and the Trust's are two hosts). 'Amiel Melburn Archive', 'Amiel Melburne Trust Archive' (the archive's own page titles) and 'banmarchive' are the census's other names for the entity; the Trust's site calls it the 'Amiel & Melburn Trust Internet Archive' (B2 F12), a name of the entity. The distinct entities below are named by the field or the census beside the entity and are never senses of its name.
distinct_entities: the Barry Amiel and Norman Melburn Trust (Registered Charity No. 281239), the archive's holder and operator (B1 F4; B2 F9–F13; ML-02); its own site is amielandmelburn.org.uk
Barry Amiel, the lawyer, and Norman Melburn, the founder (persons; B2 F9)
Common Knowledge, the cooperative that built the 2021 version (B3; B1 F5)
Bath and North East Somerset Council, whose funding finder lists the Trust (B6), a third party
the Internet Archive (archive.org), a distinct entity the Trust's phrase 'Amiel & Melburn Trust Internet Archive' does not name
The Reasoner, the New Reasoner, Universities and Left Review and New Left Review, the journals (B7 F35–F38; ML-29: the archive is 'NOT New Left Review')
the Communist Party of Great Britain, the party whose leadership ordered The Reasoner closed (B7 F35; ML-28: 'NOT the Communist Party of Great Britain's archive')
the Marxists Internet Archive, which hosts the Saville 1976 text #1725 cites beside the entity's page (D1725-02); a neighbour row of the census, built separately
the Socialist History Society, whose pamphlets the archive holds (B1 F3)
